beats.spoken: Your best password is no help if you type it into a fake site.

data.question: And what if the site is fake?

beats.spoken: That's exactly how phishing works: the site looks real, and the password goes to the attackers. And according to Germany's BSI, codes by text, email or app don't protect against real-time phishing either.
The alternative is called a passkey. It replaces the password. According to the FIDO Alliance, you unlock it just like your device: with your fingerprint, face or PIN.
The difference: with a passkey, there's nothing to type. The secret key stays on your device, and the device checks at every sign-in whether the site is genuine. A fake site gets nothing.
If a service doesn't offer passkeys yet, the BSI recommends two-factor login. And in case you lose your device, you need a backup or sync through the cloud.

data.headline: And if it's not available yet?

beats.spoken: So today: check your business email, bank and cloud storage to see whether they offer passkeys. Turn them on there first. And secure a way back in for every account.
